name: CA-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 7 points on partisan baseline
Incumbent Pete Aguilar has a large financial advantage ($4.7M raised, $3.5M on hand)
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 96%
Republican challenger Stephanie Vargas has minimal visible fundraising
model.rationale: Aguilar holds a Democratic-leaning seat, a decisive money edge, and no outside spending against him, while markets price his reelection at 96%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of about 20 points stands with only modest adjustment.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or unexpected outside spending against Aguilar would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pete Aguilar, the Democratic incumbent, seeks reelection in a Southern California district that leans Democratic by about seven points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised nearly $4.7 million and holding $3.5 million on hand, while Republican challenger Stephanie Vargas shows little visible fundraising and no outside groups are spending in the race.

Prediction markets give Aguilar roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters list the seat as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the absence of any signs of a serious challenge, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold.
